items.title: Vandemataram Movement & Home Rule in Andhra
items.body:
## Vandemataram / Swadeshi phase (1905–07)

- The **Partition of Bengal (1905)** and the all-India **Swadeshi movement** sparked the **Vandemataram agitation** in Andhra during **1905–07**.
- Extremist leader **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured the region in **1907** (including **Rajahmundry**), rousing students and youth to Swadeshi, boycott of foreign goods and national education.
- **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** was prosecuted for a **seditious article** and became one of Andhra's **earliest political prisoners**.
- **Kodi Rammurthy Naidu**, the famed Telugu **strongman and wrestler**, became a symbol of **Indian physical strength and national self-confidence** in this era of national awakening.

## Home Rule Movement (1916)

- The two **Home Rule Leagues** of 1916 — **B.G. Tilak's** (April) and **Annie Besant's** (September) — demanded **self-government within the Empire**.
- Besant's League was active across the **Madras Presidency**, including Andhra, and built the organisational base later used in Non-Cooperation.
keyPoints: Vandemataram/Swadeshi agitation in Andhra (1905–07) followed the 1905 Partition of Bengal.
Bipin Chandra Pal's 1907 tour (incl. Rajahmundry) roused Andhra youth to Swadeshi and boycott.
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was jailed for sedition — an early Andhra political prisoner.
Kodi Rammurthy Naidu, strongman/wrestler, symbolised Indian strength and national pride.
Home Rule Leagues (1916): Tilak (April) and Annie Besant (September) demanded self-government.
items.source: Wikipedia — Swadeshi movement; Bipin Chandra Pal; Kodi Rammurthy Naidu; Home Rule movement (India)

items.title: Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra (1920–22)
items.body:
## A mass movement in the districts

Gandhi's **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)** made Andhra — especially **Guntur, Krishna and Palnadu** — one of the most active regions of the Madras Presidency. Its Andhra forms included **no-revenue (no-tax) satyagrahas**, **anti-liquor (toddy-shop) picketing**, surrender of titles, and boycott of courts, councils and foreign cloth.

| Episode | Place / district | Distinctive feature | Leader |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chirala–Perala satyagraha (1921) | Guntur district | Townspeople vacated the twin towns and lived in a hut-camp called **Ramnagar** (~11 months) to resist municipal taxation | **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** (Andhra Ratna) |
| Pedanandipadu campaign (1921–22) | Guntur district | **No-revenue (no-tax) satyagraha** by peasants | **Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary**, guided by Konda Venkatappayya |
| Palnadu forest satyagraha (1921–22) | Palnadu, Guntur | Defiance of the **Pullari (grazing) tax** and forest rules; leader **martyred in 1922** | **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** |

The movement was suspended nationally after the **Chauri Chaura** incident (Feb 1922).
keyPoints: Non-Cooperation (1920–22) was strongest in Guntur, Krishna and Palnadu in Andhra.
Chirala–Perala (1921): people vacated the towns and lived in 'Ramnagar' under Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya.
Pedanandipadu (Guntur): no-revenue satyagraha led by Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary.
Palnadu: Pullari (grazing-tax)/forest satyagraha led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu, martyred 1922.
Forms: no-tax campaigns, toddy-shop picketing, boycott of courts/councils/titles.
items.source: Wikipedia — Non-Cooperation Movement; Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Kanneganti Hanumanthu

items.title: Chirala–Perala Satyagraha & Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
items.body:
## The 'Ramnagar' exodus (1921)

- The twin towns of **Chirala and Perala** (Guntur district) were raised to **municipal status**, sharply increasing taxes.
- Under **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**, the residents **abandoned the towns en masse** and built a temporary settlement of huts on the outskirts, which they named **Ramnagar**, living there for about **eleven months** to deny the municipality its revenue.
- The satyagraha became a celebrated model of **non-violent mass non-cooperation** in Andhra.

## Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya — 'Andhra Ratna'

- A **poet, orator, singer and Gandhian**, he was honoured as **Andhra Ratna** ('Jewel of Andhra').
- He was the **first Andhra leader to become a secretary of the All India Congress Committee (AICC)**.
- His powerful oratory and songs mobilised huge crowds during Non-Cooperation.
keyPoints: Chirala–Perala protested the towns' upgrade to a municipality and its higher taxes (1921).
Residents vacated the twin towns and lived in a hut-camp called 'Ramnagar' for ~11 months.
Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the satyagraha and was titled 'Andhra Ratna'.
He was the first Andhra leader to become an AICC secretary.
The agitation is a classic example of non-violent mass non-cooperation in Andhra.

items.title: Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion & Alluri Sitarama Raju (1922–24)
items.body:
## Causes

- The **1882 Madras Forest Act** curtailed the hill tribes' **podu (shifting) cultivation** and access to forest produce.
- **Forced, unpaid labour (vetti / begar)** on roads and other works deepened tribal resentment in the **Godavari agency (Manyam)** tracts.

## Course & end

- Led by **Alluri Sitarama Raju**, revered as **'Manyam Veerudu'** (Hero of the Jungle), the revolt began in **August 1922**.
- Rebels used **guerrilla tactics**, raiding police stations (e.g. **Chintapalle, Krishnadevipeta, Rajavommangi**) to seize arms.
- The British deployed the **Malabar Special Police**; the rebellion ended with Raju's **capture and killing on 7 May 1924**.
- Note: this was an **armed tribal revolt**, distinct from the Gandhian, non-violent Non-Cooperation campaigns elsewhere in Andhra.
keyPoints: Rampa/Manyam Rebellion (Aug 1922 – May 1924) was an armed tribal revolt in the Godavari agency.
Causes: 1882 Madras Forest Act curbing podu cultivation, plus forced labour (vetti/begar).
Led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, known as 'Manyam Veerudu'.
Guerrilla raids on police stations (Chintapalle, Krishnadevipeta, Rajavommangi) for arms.
Raju was captured and shot dead on 7 May 1924, ending the rebellion.
items.source: Wikipedia — Rampa Rebellion of 1922; Alluri Sitarama Raju

items.title: Civil Disobedience & Quit India in Andhra
items.body:
## Salt Satyagraha / Civil Disobedience (1930)

- Following Gandhi's **Dandi March (1930)**, Andhra's long **eastern coastline** made **salt-making from sea water and coastal salt marches** the natural form of the salt satyagraha, along the **Krishna–Godavari and other coastal districts**.
- **Tanguturi Prakasam** (later 'Andhra Kesari', famed for baring his chest before the **Simon Commission** in Madras, 1928) and other Congress leaders were active in this phase.

## Quit India Movement (1942)

- Gandhi's **'Do or Die'** call (**8 August 1942**, Bombay) launched Quit India.
- With the top leadership jailed, it became a **largely spontaneous, decentralised revolt**; in Andhra it took the form of **hartals, disruption of communications, attacks on symbols of British authority and mass arrests**.
keyPoints: Salt Satyagraha (1930) in Andhra used coastal salt-making along the Krishna–Godavari seaboard.
Tanguturi Prakasam ('Andhra Kesari') was prominent; he had bared his chest to the Simon Commission (1928).
Quit India began with Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call on 8 August 1942.
In Andhra, 1942 saw hartals, attacks on British symbols and large-scale arrests.
With leaders imprisoned, the 1942 movement was largely spontaneous and decentralised.
items.source: Wikipedia — Salt March; Quit India Movement; Tanguturi Prakasam

items.title: Andhra Leaders of the Freedom Struggle — Titles at a Glance
items.body:
## Who was who

| Leader | Title | Chiefly known for |
|---|---|---|
| **Alluri Sitarama Raju** | Manyam Veerudu | Armed Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion, 1922–24 |
| **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** | Andhra Ratna | Chirala–Perala satyagraha; first Andhra AICC secretary |
| **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** | — (Palnadu martyr) | Palnadu forest/Pullari satyagraha; martyred 1922 |
| **Konda Venkatappayya** | Desabhakta | Lawyer–Congress organiser of Non-Cooperation campaigns |
| **Tanguturi Prakasam** | Andhra Kesari | Defiance of the Simon Commission (1928); salt satyagraha |
| **Garimella Satyanarayana** | — (nationalist poet) | Patriotic songs mobilising the masses; jailed repeatedly |
| **Kodi Rammurthy Naidu** | — (strongman) | Feats of strength symbolising national self-confidence |

Together they gave the Andhra freedom struggle its **peasant, tribal, literary and organisational** dimensions.
keyPoints: Alluri Sitarama Raju = 'Manyam Veerudu' (Rampa Rebellion).
Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya = 'Andhra Ratna' (Chirala–Perala).
Konda Venkatappayya = 'Desabhakta'; Tanguturi Prakasam = 'Andhra Kesari'.
Kanneganti Hanumanthu led and was martyred in the Palnadu satyagraha (1922).
Garimella Satyanarayana was the nationalist poet jailed for his patriotic songs.
items.mnemonic: Titles: Raju=Manyam Veerudu, Duggirala=Andhra Ratna, Konda=Desabhakta, Prakasam=Andhra Kesari.
items.source: Wikipedia — Alluri Sitarama Raju; Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Kanneganti Hanumanthu; Konda Venkatappayya; Tanguturi Prakasam; Garimella Satyanarayana
